title: [Performance] Fuse GDN metadata construction for mixed batches
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

GDN metadata preparation launches separate indexing, partitioning, padding and shared-convolution-output clearing operators. This change combines those device operations in one Triton launch before model execution, reusing the existing graph buffers. Metadata preparation remains outside model graphs.

The fused host-metadata builder handles ordinary decode, variable speculative lengths, prefill/decode mixtures, and mixtures of speculative and non-speculative requests. It shares the existing CPU batch classification and decode descriptor helpers, and runs after request normalization. The kernel generates the device tensors; common builder code attaches the decode descriptors. Mixed speculative batches transfer one compact CPU partition instead of a mask and two sequence-index arrays, and each request writes its token range directly from the known partition offsets, without token-to-request searches, token-mask expansion or sorting. Homogeneous batches need no partition transfer.

The original ordinary/speculative grouping semantics, PCP context and graph-padding behavior are preserved. Unsupported cache/convolution layouts and capture use the original implementation. There are no model-name checks, new configuration flags or device-to-host synchronizations.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Lower metadata preparation overhead for GDN host-metadata paths using aligned Mamba caches. Release note: `release_notes/fragments/19954.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

**Operator accuracy — fused vs. unfused (2026-10-29)**

Ascend950DT x1, using the fixed-vLLM environment of the first GPQA run. Both paths used identical inputs: the unfused reference disabled `_build_fused_metadata` to use the original builder, while the fused path ran the Triton kernel. Every metadata tensor and descriptor field was compared.

| Metric | Unfused | Fused |
|---|---:|---:|
| Exact match to unfused metadata | Reference | 26/26 cases (100%) |

Tensor comparison used `rtol=0, atol=0`. Coverage included ordinary and speculative decode, variable draft lengths, prefill/decode mixtures, strided inputs, changing batch counts, graph padding and shared-output clearing, with both NONE and FULL_DECODE_ONLY configured.

**GPQA Diamond accuracy — first paired run (2026-10-28)**

GLM-5.3-Flash (`GLM-5.3-Flash-W8A8-MXFP8-0918`), W8A8-MXFP8 with BF16 KDA projections, on Ascend950DT x8 with TP8+EP. Serving used FP8 KV, aligned Mamba caches, MTP3, FULL_DECODE_ONLY and the V2 runner; metadata fusion remained outside model graphs.

AISBench : all 198 Diamond questions, zero-shot CoT chat prompt, fixed cyclic answer-option permutation, temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, seed=1024, max_tokens=131072, concurrency=32, and the weight template's default Max reasoning effort. Requests ended naturally or at the token limit; warmup was excluded.

| Metric | Unfused | Fused |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPQA Diamond accuracy | 90.91% | 90.91% |
| Correct answers | 180/198 | 180/198 |

Both variants used the same PR source and serving/evaluation settings. The evaluation harness forced `_build_fused_metadata` to return `None` for the unfused variant and called the original fused entry for the fused variant. CPU route counters and API termination recording did not change model requests or scoring. No profiler or synchronized timing was used in this accuracy run.

Earlier synthetic **metadata-only** measurements on one NPU: 16 requests, MTP3, aligned cache, FULL_DECODE_ONLY configured, 20 warmups, three alternating rounds of 50 samples, synchronization before/after each build, median of round means. These are not model throughput or ITL measurements.

| Batch | Generic | Fused | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Uniform speculative decode | 0.612 ms | 0.208 ms | 66.1% |
| Variable speculative lengths | 0.576 ms | 0.210 ms | 63.5% |
| Ordinary decode + prefill | 0.582 ms | 0.451 ms | 22.6% |
| Speculative decode + prefill + ordinary decode | 0.808 ms | 0.569 ms | 29.6% |

A separate skewed-batch check used 15 four-token speculative requests plus one prefill of 4,097, 32,769 or 131,073 tokens. Complete metadata matched the generic builder. The direct per-request token writes took 0.548/0.568/0.634 ms versus 0.553/0.572/0.637 ms for the previous token-search implementation in the same process; no regression was observed in these samples.

GLM-5.3-Flash, Ascend950DT x8, TP8+EP, 131072 input /1024 output, MTP3, aligned cache, int8 KV, FULL_DECODE_ONLY; physical prefix-cache hit rate 99.3164%.

| Concurrency | Measurement | Generic | Fused | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 | Metadata stage, synchronized | 2.249 ms | 0.943 ms | -58.05% |
| 10 | Natural step interval | 29.761 ms | 29.133 ms | -2.11% |
| 10 | Uninstrumented decode throughput | 1193.19 token/s | 1216.07 token/s | +1.92% |
| 32 | Metadata stage, synchronized | 2.289 ms | 0.952 ms | -58.42% |
| 32 | Natural step interval | 41.751 ms | 41.606 ms | -0.35% |
| 32 | Uninstrumented decode throughput | 2876.00 token/s | 2881.35 token/s | +0.19% |
| 64 | Metadata stage, synchronized | 2.282 ms | 0.974 ms | -57.32% |
| 64 | Natural step interval | 55.324 ms | 55.198 ms | -0.23% |
| 64 | Uninstrumented decode throughput | 4397.05 token/s | 4406.65 token/s | +0.22% |

Three rounds per metric. Metadata averages 3x64x8 synchronized samples, excluding the initial wait. Natural step cadence uses consecutive main-stream target-entry events without per-step synchronization. Throughput uses separate uninstrumented rounds from every request emitting at least 128 tokens until first completion, excluding startup backlog and reduced-concurrency tails. Outputs, cache counts and scheduled work matched. The small end-to-end changes are descriptive, without a claim of statistical significance.
